1. KHAJARAHAMATULLA S Counsel for the Respondent(S):
1. GP FOR LAND ACQUISITION

The Court made the following order:
Heard Sri S. Khajarahamatulla, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondents.

2. The contention of the petitioners in the instant writ petition is to the endorsement passed in Rc.(C) No.49/2017 dated 12-06-2017 by the 3rd respondent refusing to refer the matter to the Civil Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") for determination of compensation in respect of the land in Sy.No.364/2P and 364/3P, to an extent of Ac.2.45 cents in Reach No.13,
situated at Penubarthi Village, Rapur Mandal, SPSR Nellore District.
3. It is contended that the lands, were acquired for the purpose of the Kandaleru Reservoir project and compensation was paid.

sentences.text: 4. Thereafter, in 2016, seeking enhancement of compensation, the applicant approached the authorities to refer the issue to the competent Civil Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The petitioners submitted a representation requesting the authorities to refer the matter to the competent Civil Court under Section 18 of the Act for the determination of enhanced compensation.
However, the said request was rejected by way of the endorsement.
Hence, the present writ petition.
5. The respondents filed a counter-affidavit stating that the lands were assigned lands and that ex gratia was also paid.

After 15 years, the petitioners, having received ex gratia, filed an application for reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, which was rejected.
The writ petition is not maintainable.

6. The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondents would submit that no award in terms of the provisions of the Act in respect of the subject lands was passed having regard to the fact that the lands were assigned lands, the petitioners is only eligible for grant of ex gratia and thus cannot seek reference under Section 18 of the Act.
In respect of Patta lands, awards were passed and compensation was also paid to the persons from whom the lands were acquired.
The petitioners was paid ex-gratia amount of Rs.25,934/-.

7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition urges that, in any event, reference under Section 18 of the Act can be made only in case any person interested in the lands, who has not accepted the award, may, by written application to the Collector, require that the Collector refer the matter to the Court.
There is a time limitation in seeking such a reference.
The limitation would be within six weeks from the date of the award.
Whereas, in this case, after 15 years from the grant of ex-gratia, the petitioners sought reference under Section 18 of the Act which is not maintainable.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioners relies on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Manharlal Shivlal Panchal vs. The Deputy Collector & Special Land Acquisition Officer1.
9.

entities.text: Manharlal Shivlal Panchal vs. The Deputy Collector & Special Land Acquisition Officer1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considered the submissions.
The judgment of the Supreme Court relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner is distinguishable.

Having regard to the fact that the land owners in the said case have challenged the land acquisition proceedings and award under Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which culminated in dismissal of the Special Leave Petition vide order dated 11.04.2013.
Thereafter, reference applications were filed on 01.07.2013.

After dismissal of the SLPs on 11.04.2013, pursuant to the liberty granted by the High Court while dismissing the writ petition,
the applications under Section 18 of the Act were filed within a period of six months from the date of such liberty granted by the High Court on 01.07.2013.
On account of such liberty being granted in favour of the petitioners therein, the applications seeking enhancement of compensation were held to be maintainable.

sentences.text: Whereas, in the present case, the petitioners, after receiving the ex gratia amount, having kept silent for 15 years, sought reference under the Act.

In other words, the action of the claimants amounts to acceptance of the Civil Appeal No.9004 of 2022 dated 12.12.2022 amount of compensation, and having acquiesced in the matter, it is not justifiable to seek Reference under Sec.18 of the Act, having regard to the period of limitation prescribed under the statute.

11. Thus, the petitioners has not made out any justifiable cause for entertaining such a belated application under Sec.18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the relief sought by the petitioner does not merit consideration.
12. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs

As a sequel,
miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
